requirements.requirement: Create on node1 a local certificate authority named “OS Comparison Root CA”.
requirements.summary: The target paths were initially absent. The executor then created a self-signed certificate with the exact requested common name, critical CA constraints and certificate-signing usage. Direct checks show that its locally stored private key matches the certificate; the same certificate and key remained intact after restart.

requirements.requirement: Install that certificate as a trusted system certificate authority on node1.
requirements.summary: The certificate appears in the system trust store as an anchor, and a leaf certificate signed by it verifies successfully through the system CA bundle. Both trust-anchor status and functional verification were repeated successfully after node1 restarted.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: node1 was healthy with boot ID fb2aa416-d036-46d3-aeb8-30c65a01cb34, acknowledged the scheduled restart, returned running with boot ID 5072428f-60d5-4a45-9699-eccbb7321e63, and retained functional CA trust. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the identity change.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The lasting key, certificate, permissions, and regenerated trust bundle from cmd-dbd53f3d29564f26 directly implement the task. The reboot scheduled by cmd-3aa08bfc6b414f55 served the mandatory restart protocol. Probe artifacts created by cmd-5858052c18d34365 and cmd-807766e8afdd4400 were bounded and removed by traps. Post-execution observations show no failed services, damaged package state, new exposure, or abandoned temporary files; socket and temporary-directory differences are normal consequences of the verified reboot.
